ed43qr.q: The driver must adjust speed according to the characteristics of the vehicle.
ed43qr.why: Vehicle characteristics such as weight, braking and stability affect stopping distance, so speed must be adapted to them.

1nk8jer.q: The driver must adjust speed according to the condition of the vehicle.
1nk8jer.why: A vehicle in poor condition (brakes, tyres, suspension) needs a lower speed. The vehicle's condition is a factor the law requires you to consider.

1pyt9uc.q: The driver must adjust speed according to the load of the vehicle.
1pyt9uc.why: The load changes weight, centre of gravity and braking distance, so speed must be adjusted to it.

w50h2k.q: The driver must adjust speed according to the characteristics of the road.
w50h2k.why: Road width, bends, gradient and surface affect safety, so speed must be adapted to the road's characteristics.

1pnr401.q: The driver must adjust speed according to the conditions of the road.
1pnr401.why: A wet, uneven, icy or obstructed road surface requires lower speed.

9vgvgr.q: The driver must adjust speed according to traffic conditions.
9vgvgr.why: Heavy or irregular traffic requires adapting speed to avoid collisions and obstruction.

1jsi70f.q: The driver must adjust speed so as not to endanger property.
1jsi70f.why: Speed must be controlled so that it does not create a risk of damage to property, as well as to people.

1c1d4zu.q: The driver must adjust speed so as not to endanger people.
1c1d4zu.why: The driver must keep speed at a level that does not put people's safety at risk.

hs4tvo.q: The driver must adjust speed so as not to cause disorder to traffic.
hs4tvo.why: Speed must not cause obstruction or disorder in traffic, for example through sudden braking or manoeuvres.

tz8z2q.q: The driver must adjust speed within the maximum limits allowed.
tz8z2q.why: Maximum speed limits must never be exceeded; they are the ceiling within which you set your speed.

13iigsx.q: The driver must adjust speed so as to comply with the restrictions imposed.
13iigsx.why: The driver must obey speed restrictions imposed by signs or by the authorities.

ubhmdu.q: The driver must adjust speed according to weather conditions.
ubhmdu.why: Rain, fog, snow or wind reduce grip and visibility, so speed must be reduced.

1u0kqar.q: The driver must adjust speed taking into account the maximum limits only.
1u0kqar.why: Maximum limits alone are not enough: speed must also always be adapted to the vehicle, road, traffic and weather.

fhtgcs.q: The driver must adjust speed according to his or her own driving skill.
fhtgcs.why: The law looks at the vehicle, load, road, traffic and weather, not at the driver's personal skill.

1smrkg3.q: The driver must adjust speed according to the brand of the tyres.
1smrkg3.why: Tyre brand is not a legal criterion; what matters is tyre condition and the state of the road and vehicle.

w8y7j4.q: The driver must adjust speed according to the distance of the place to be reached.
w8y7j4.why: The distance still to travel does not affect safety and is not a criterion for setting speed.

a0shgq.q: The driver must always keep control of the vehicle.
a0shgq.why: The driver must always be able to control the vehicle and carry out every necessary manoeuvre safely.

4afepl.q: The driver must always be able to stop the vehicle safely.
4afepl.why: The stopping distance must always allow a safe stop before any foreseeable obstacle.

13m2p4t.q: The driver must be able to stop the vehicle within the field of vision and in safe conditions.
13m2p4t.why: You must be able to stop within the distance you can see ahead, so speed must drop when visibility is limited.

impg9.q: It is mandatory to adjust speed on bends.
impg9.why: On bends visibility is reduced and stability is lower, so speed must be adjusted.

1eldnhp.q: It is mandatory to adjust speed on stretches of road with limited visibility.
1eldnhp.why: With limited visibility you cannot see obstacles in time, so speed must be reduced to be able to stop.

rue1i0.q: It is mandatory to adjust speed near intersections.
rue1i0.why: Other vehicles or pedestrians may appear at intersections, so speed must be moderated.

1w9939o.q: It is mandatory to adjust speed near schools.
1w9939o.why: Children may cross suddenly near schools, so speed must be adjusted.

7hnqbi.q: It is mandatory to adjust speed near places frequented by children.
7hnqbi.why: Children behave unpredictably, so the Code requires you to moderate speed where they are present.

qzrzx2.q: It is mandatory to adjust speed on steep descents.
qzrzx2.why: On steep descents braking distance increases and brakes overheat, so speed must be adjusted.

1pht9si.q: It is mandatory to adjust speed in narrow passages.
1pht9si.why: Manoeuvring space is limited in narrow passages, so speed must be moderated.

k8khbx.q: It is mandatory to adjust speed in obstructed passages.
k8khbx.why: In obstructed passages you need a reduced speed to avoid the obstacles or stop in time.

165wlkf.q: It is mandatory to adjust speed at night.
165wlkf.why: Visibility is poorer at night, so speed must be adjusted to allow stopping within the illuminated distance.

rqcl81.q: It is mandatory to adjust speed when passing through built-up areas.
rqcl81.why: Built-up areas (centri abitati) have pedestrians, junctions and frequent hazards, so speed must be adjusted.

1u6wzqd.q: It is mandatory to adjust speed on stretches of road lined with buildings.
1u6wzqd.why: Pedestrians or vehicles may emerge suddenly from beside buildings, so speed must be moderated.

1435d6u.q: It is mandatory to reduce speed when it is difficult to pass other vehicles.
1435d6u.why: When passing oncoming vehicles is difficult, the driver must slow down and, if needed, stop.

dib2jf.q: It is mandatory to adjust speed in fog or mist.
dib2jf.why: Fog and mist reduce visibility, so speed must be lowered to be able to stop the vehicle.

13fwvx5.q: It is mandatory to adjust speed on stretches of road covered with snow.
13fwvx5.why: Snow reduces grip and lengthens braking distance, so speed must be adjusted.

xgvc5q.q: It is mandatory to adjust speed on stretches of road covered with ice.
xgvc5q.why: Ice greatly reduces grip and makes braking and steering difficult, so speed must be adjusted.

19aghl8.q: It is mandatory to reduce speed on a one-way road.
19aghl8.why: A one-way road does not in itself require a lower speed; the normal limit applies and you adapt to conditions.

13ealw.q: It is mandatory to reduce speed outside built-up areas.
13ealw.why: Limits are higher outside built-up areas; there is no general obligation to reduce speed there.

ixgz5n.q: It is mandatory to reduce speed on provincial roads.
ixgz5n.why: The type of road, such as a provincial road, does not by itself require slowing down; the limit and conditions decide.

1teg51i.q: It is mandatory to adjust speed during the day but not at night.
1teg51i.why: Speed must be adjusted at all times, including at night when visibility is worse.

1dsignd.q: It is mandatory to adjust speed on straight stretches and not on bends.
1dsignd.why: The opposite is true: speed must especially be adjusted on bends, where visibility and stability are reduced.

1anrawq.q: It is mandatory to reduce speed on uphill roads.
1anrawq.why: An uphill road does not in itself require slowing down; the duty applies to steep descents and other hazardous situations.

4qo246.q: It is mandatory to reduce speed in the presence of any road sign.
4qo246.why: Not every sign requires slowing down; only danger signs, speed limits or situations that call for it do.

zfhbkm.q: It is mandatory to reduce speed only in the presence of traffic officers.
zfhbkm.why: Speed must be adjusted to conditions at all times, not only when traffic officers are present.

1l1ri9l.q: It is mandatory to adjust speed on secondary extra-urban roads but not on main ones.
1l1ri9l.why: Speed must be adjusted on every type of road, including main extra-urban roads.

xcnrs.q: It is mandatory to reduce speed only if the car is unladen.
xcnrs.why: Load affects braking, but there is no rule to slow down only when the car is empty.

8rzfcn.q: It is mandatory to reduce speed near speed cameras.
8rzfcn.why: The duty is to respect speed limits at all times, not to slow down only near speed cameras (autovelox).

jhoj68.q: It is mandatory to reduce speed and, if necessary, stop when passing other vehicles is difficult.
jhoj68.why: When passing other vehicles is awkward, you must slow down and stop if necessary to let them through.

1birdu6.q: It is mandatory to reduce speed and, if necessary, stop near pedestrian crossings.
1birdu6.why: Near pedestrian crossings you must slow down and stop if needed to give way to pedestrians.

uixdtt.q: It is mandatory to reduce speed and, if necessary, stop when pedestrians on your path are slow to move aside.
uixdtt.why: If pedestrians on your path are slow to get out of the way, you must slow down and stop if necessary.

vo6sa6.q: It is mandatory to reduce speed and, if necessary, stop when pedestrians on your path show signs of uncertainty.
vo6sa6.why: When pedestrians on your path seem unsure, you must slow down and stop if necessary.

1q2v30v.q: It is mandatory to reduce speed and, if necessary, stop when animals on the road show signs of fear.
1q2v30v.why: Frightened animals are unpredictable, so you must slow down and stop if necessary.

x66cva.q: It is mandatory to reduce speed and, if necessary, stop when dazzled.
x66cva.why: When dazzled you cannot see the road, so you must slow down and stop if necessary.

q5ck2x.q: It is mandatory to reduce speed and, if necessary, stop at driveways.
q5ck2x.why: There is no general obligation to slow down and stop at driveways (passi carrabili).

1piihnd.q: It is mandatory to reduce speed and, if necessary, stop near bus stops.
1piihnd.why: Bus stops do not in themselves create an obligation to slow down and stop.

1r55glf.q: It is mandatory to reduce speed and, if necessary, stop every time you travel over an overpass.
1r55glf.why: Driving over an overpass does not require slowing down and stopping; normal limits and conditions apply.

179qa55.q: It is mandatory to reduce speed and, if necessary, stop near speed cameras.
179qa55.why: Limits must be respected at all times; there is no duty to slow down and stop near speed cameras (autovelox).

c3ssxf.q: It is mandatory to reduce speed and, if necessary, stop at any road sign.
c3ssxf.why: Only certain signs (danger signs, STOP, limits) require slowing or stopping, not just any sign.

ocmnme.q: It is mandatory to reduce speed and, if necessary, stop when leaving built-up areas.
ocmnme.why: When leaving a built-up area limits normally rise; there is no duty to slow down and stop.

1l22z0.q: The maximum speed limit for a car on motorways is ordinarily 130 km/h.
1l22z0.why: On motorways (autostrade) the ordinary limit for cars is 130 km/h.

1p4jyn.q: The maximum speed limit for a car on main extra-urban roads is ordinarily 110 km/h.
1p4jyn.why: On main extra-urban roads (strade extraurbane principali) the ordinary limit for cars is 110 km/h.

5szsqo.q: The maximum speed limit for a car on secondary extra-urban roads is 90 km/h.
5szsqo.why: On secondary extra-urban roads (strade extraurbane secondarie) the limit for cars is 90 km/h.

1gm4k5n.q: The maximum speed limit for a car in built-up areas is ordinarily 50 km/h.
1gm4k5n.why: In built-up areas (centri abitati) the ordinary limit is 50 km/h unless signs say otherwise.

1xtofr4.q: The maximum speed limit for a motor vehicle up to 3.5 tonnes on motorways is ordinarily 130 km/h.
1xtofr4.why: Motor vehicles up to 3.5 tonnes gross weight follow the ordinary motorway limit of 130 km/h.

1o1dpz.q: The maximum speed limit for a lorry up to 3.5 tonnes on main extra-urban roads is 110 km/h.
1o1dpz.why: Lorries (autocarri) up to 3.5 tonnes may travel at 110 km/h on main extra-urban roads.

y5mjk4.q: The maximum speed limit for a motor vehicle up to 3.5 tonnes on secondary extra-urban roads is 90 km/h.
y5mjk4.why: On secondary extra-urban roads, motor vehicles up to 3.5 tonnes have a 90 km/h limit.

1mflvb3.q: The maximum speed limit for a motorcycle in built-up areas is ordinarily 50 km/h.
1mflvb3.why: The ordinary 50 km/h limit in built-up areas also applies to motorcycles.

h5dnfg.q: The maximum speed limit for a car, where a specific sign is present, on motorway sections with particular characteristics is 150 km/h.
h5dnfg.why: On motorway sections with particular design features and a specific sign, the limit can rise to 150 km/h.

3htmuu.q: The maximum speed limit for a car, where signs are present, on an urban road with particular characteristics is 70 km/h.
3htmuu.why: On urban roads with special characteristics and proper signs, the limit can be 70 km/h.

j0h0py.q: The maximum speed limit for a car on motorways in case of precipitation is 110 km/h.
j0h0py.why: In rain or other precipitation the motorway limit drops from 130 to 110 km/h.

o2e5nj.q: The maximum speed limit for a car on main extra-urban roads in case of precipitation is 90 km/h.
o2e5nj.why: In precipitation the limit on main extra-urban roads drops from 110 to 90 km/h.

ye88pv.q: The maximum speed limit for mopeds is 45 km/h.
ye88pv.why: Mopeds (ciclomotori) may not exceed 45 km/h on any road.

1eg8mb7.q: The maximum speed limit for heavy quadricycles outside built-up areas is 80 km/h.
1eg8mb7.why: Heavy quadricycles (quadricicli non leggeri) outside built-up areas have an 80 km/h limit.

fbkbl7.q: The maximum speed limit for a wheeled agricultural machine is 40 km/h.
fbkbl7.why: Wheeled agricultural machines (macchine agricole) may not exceed 40 km/h.

106h2kv.q: The maximum speed limit for a wheeled operating machine is 40 km/h.
106h2kv.why: Wheeled operating machines (macchine operatrici) may not exceed 40 km/h.

1pgnq59.q: The maximum speed limit for a car on any motorway is 150 km/h.
1pgnq59.why: The ordinary motorway limit is 130 km/h; 150 km/h applies only on suitable sections where signed.

1qui0t1.q: The maximum speed limit for a car on a main extra-urban road is 90 km/h.
1qui0t1.why: On main extra-urban roads the limit is 110 km/h; 90 km/h applies in precipitation or on secondary roads.

yn3h1z.q: The maximum speed limit for a car on a secondary extra-urban road is 70 km/h.
yn3h1z.why: On secondary extra-urban roads the limit for cars is 90 km/h, not 70.

1fdvshx.q: The maximum speed limit for a car in built-up areas is always 70 km/h.
1fdvshx.why: In built-up areas the ordinary limit is 50 km/h; 70 km/h applies only on special roads with signs.

fpmmtr.q: The maximum speed limit for a car in built-up areas is always 50 km/h.
fpmmtr.why: 50 km/h is the ordinary limit, not an absolute one: signs can set it lower (30) or higher (70 km/h).

ddo63.q: The maximum speed limit for quadricycles outside built-up areas is 70 km/h.
ddo63.why: Outside built-up areas heavy quadricycles have an 80 km/h limit, not 70.

16swu3s.q: The maximum speed limit for lorries in built-up areas is 40 km/h.
16swu3s.why: In built-up areas lorries follow the general limit of 50 km/h, not 40.

n137il.q: The maximum speed limit for a lorry with a gross weight up to 3.5 tonnes on motorways is 120 km/h.
n137il.why: A lorry up to 3.5 tonnes on motorways has the ordinary limit of 130 km/h, not 120.

fjfc8j.q: The maximum speed limit for a motor vehicle up to 3.5 tonnes on main extra-urban roads is 80 km/h.
fjfc8j.why: On main extra-urban roads motor vehicles up to 3.5 tonnes may travel at 110 km/h, not 80.

e8h5xo.q: The maximum speed limit for a motor vehicle up to 3.5 tonnes in built-up areas is 40 km/h.
e8h5xo.why: In built-up areas the limit for motor vehicles up to 3.5 tonnes is 50 km/h, not 40.

13qh4ed.q: The maximum speed limit for any vehicle in built-up areas is 60 km/h.
13qh4ed.why: The ordinary limit in built-up areas is 50 km/h; 60 km/h is not a limit set by the Code.

1ckahe5.q: The maximum speed limit for an agricultural machine with tyres is 50 km/h.
1ckahe5.why: Agricultural machines with tyres may not exceed 40 km/h, not 50.

sivryc.q: The maximum speed limit for a wheeled operating machine is 50 km/h.
sivryc.why: Wheeled operating machines may not exceed 40 km/h, not 50.

1vzgb1w.q: The speed limit on motorways for those who have held a licence for less than 3 years is 100 km/h.
1vzgb1w.why: Drivers licensed for less than 3 years (neopatentati) may not exceed 100 km/h on motorways.

ssa2u1.q: The speed limit on main extra-urban roads for those who have held a licence for less than 3 years is 90 km/h.
ssa2u1.why: New drivers (neopatentati) are limited to 90 km/h on main extra-urban roads, lower than the normal 110 km/h.

2x542h.q: Driving at high speed affects fuel consumption and environmental pollution.
2x542h.why: The faster you drive, the more fuel you burn and the more pollutants the vehicle emits.

10qxh7w.q: Sudden changes of speed lead to higher fuel consumption.
10qxh7w.why: Harsh acceleration and braking use more fuel than smooth, steady driving.

zlw8zu.q: Speed in a bend affects the vehicle's road holding.
zlw8zu.why: The faster you take a bend, the greater the centrifugal force and the less grip (tenuta di strada) the vehicle has.

6bpho0.q: Excessive speed in a bend can cause the vehicle to overturn.
6bpho0.why: Too much speed in a bend increases centrifugal force and can make the vehicle skid or roll over.

u30qyb.q: Bends must be driven with the clutch pedal pressed down.
u30qyb.why: You do not hold the clutch down in a bend. Slow down beforehand and keep the gear engaged to stay in control.

ltvll7.q: The speed limit on motorways for those who have held a licence for less than three years is 110 km/h.
ltvll7.why: New drivers (neopatentati) are limited to 100 km/h on motorways, not 110.

y468lm.q: The speed limit on main extra-urban roads for those who have held a licence for less than 3 years is 110 km/h.
y468lm.why: New drivers are limited to 90 km/h on main extra-urban roads; 110 km/h is the ordinary limit for everyone else.

fxyatk.q: The maximum speed limit on motorways is ordinarily 130 km/h for cars with a light trailer (carrello appendice).
fxyatk.why: A light appendage trailer (carrello appendice) does not lower the limit: the car keeps the normal motorway limit of 130 km/h.

2096g5.q: The maximum speed limit on motorways is 80 km/h for cars with a trailer.
2096g5.why: Cars towing a trailer (rimorchio) may not exceed 80 km/h on motorways.

zd4ti0.q: The maximum speed limit on motorways is ordinarily 130 km/h for motorcycles.
zd4ti0.why: Motorcycles follow the same limits as cars, so 130 km/h on motorways.

niujeu.q: The maximum speed limit on motorways is ordinarily 130 km/h for motorhomes (autocaravan) with a gross mass of up to 3.5 tonnes.
niujeu.why: Motorhomes (autocaravan) up to 3.5 tonnes gross mass are subject to the ordinary motorway limit of 130 km/h.

ifd6wf.q: The maximum speed limit on motorways is 80 km/h for a car towing a caravan.
ifd6wf.why: A car towing a caravan is limited to 80 km/h on motorways.

6fgwx.q: The maximum speed limit on main extra-urban roads is ordinarily 110 km/h for motorcycles.
6fgwx.why: On main extra-urban roads motorcycles follow the ordinary limit of 110 km/h.

ldl5tu.q: The maximum speed limit on main extra-urban roads is 110 km/h for cars with a light trailer (carrello appendice).
ldl5tu.why: With a light appendage trailer (carrello appendice) the normal road limit applies: 110 km/h on main extra-urban roads.

7eoqjd.q: The maximum speed limit on main extra-urban roads is 70 km/h for cars with a trailer for carrying boats.
7eoqjd.why: Cars towing any trailer, including a boat trailer, may not exceed 70 km/h on main extra-urban roads.

18twvxm.q: The maximum speed limit on secondary extra-urban roads is 90 km/h for motorcycles.
18twvxm.why: Motorcycles may travel at 90 km/h on secondary extra-urban roads, the same as cars.

11ehluw.q: The maximum speed limit on secondary extra-urban roads is 70 km/h for a car towing a caravan with a gross mass of 900 kilograms.
11ehluw.why: A car towing a caravan or trailer is limited to 70 km/h on secondary extra-urban roads.

10v4ndx.q: The maximum speed limit on motorways is 130 km/h for cars with a trailer.
10v4ndx.why: With a trailer the motorway limit drops to 80 km/h; 130 km/h applies only without one.

yl7re1.q: The maximum speed limit on motorways is 90 km/h for motorcycles.
yl7re1.why: Motorcycles may travel up to 130 km/h on motorways, not 90.

1g1lttc.q: The maximum speed limit on motorways is 90 km/h for motorhomes (autocaravan).
1g1lttc.why: Motorhomes (autocaravan) up to 3.5 t follow the ordinary motorway limit of 130 km/h, not 90.

hwqw7h.q: The maximum speed limit on motorways is 70 km/h for a car towing a caravan.
hwqw7h.why: A car towing a caravan may go up to 80 km/h on motorways, not 70.

115ax70.q: The maximum speed limit on motorways is 120 km/h for cars with a light trailer (carrello appendice) in the rain.
115ax70.why: In rain the motorway limit is 110 km/h, and a light appendage trailer (carrello appendice) does not change that.

1d33yc1.q: The maximum speed limit on main extra-urban roads is 100 km/h for motorcycles.
1d33yc1.why: Motorcycles may travel up to 110 km/h on main extra-urban roads, not 100.

10r25fz.q: The maximum speed limit on main extra-urban roads is 80 km/h for cars with a trailer for carrying boats.
10r25fz.why: With any trailer the limit on main extra-urban roads is 70 km/h, not 80.

1vhat3k.q: The maximum speed limit on secondary extra-urban roads is 70 km/h for motorcycles.
1vhat3k.why: Motorcycles may go up to 90 km/h on secondary extra-urban roads; 70 km/h applies to vehicles towing a trailer.

1sejkvi.q: The speed of vehicles must be regulated so as not to obstruct traffic.
1sejkvi.why: Drivers must adjust their speed so they do not obstruct or hold up the flow of traffic.

16nwrsl.q: It is mandatory to reduce speed and, if necessary, stop at junctions to let vehicles that have right of way pass.
16nwrsl.why: At junctions you must slow down and, if necessary, stop to give way to vehicles with priority.

13u6uco.q: It is mandatory to reduce speed and, if necessary, stop from half an hour before sunset to half an hour after sunrise.
13u6uco.why: The duty to slow down or stop depends on specific situations such as junctions, pedestrians or obstacles, not on the time of day.

ky2efd.q: You are required to regulate your speed according to the type of engine fuel.
ky2efd.why: Speed is adjusted to road, traffic, weather, vehicle and load, not to the fuel type of the engine.

h6jtjl.q: You are required to regulate your speed according to the speed of the vehicles following you.
h6jtjl.why: You regulate speed according to road and traffic conditions, not to the speed of the vehicles behind you.

2tlseu.q: You are required to regulate your speed according to the type of gearbox.
2tlseu.why: The type of gearbox is not a factor the law lists for adjusting your speed.

1o6iza.q: Speed must be moderate on stretches of road with restricted visibility.
1o6iza.why: Where visibility is limited you must keep your speed moderate so you can stop safely.

71ftwd.q: You must keep a speed that does not endanger road safety.
71ftwd.why: Your speed must never create a danger to road safety.

1otnffn.q: You must keep a speed that allows you to deal safely with unexpected events.
1otnffn.why: You must be able to react safely to the unexpected, so your speed has to allow for that.

1vgnd4g.q: You must keep a speed suited to your own physical and mental condition.
1vgnd4g.why: Tiredness or reduced physical and mental ability means you must lower your speed accordingly.

44v4k2.q: It is the driver's duty to regulate speed in relation to the vehicle's load.
44v4k2.why: The load affects braking and stability, so the driver must adjust speed to it.

1ibbuyg.q: You must keep a speed regulated according to the time you have available.
1ibbuyg.why: Being in a hurry or having limited time is not a legitimate reason to set your speed.

6a80ya.q: Speed must be moderate outside built-up areas.
6a80ya.why: The duty to moderate speed applies in specific situations, not as a blanket rule outside built-up areas, where limits are higher.

wrelvo.q: Where a specific sign is present, the maximum permitted speed may be 150 km/h on stretches of motorway with particular characteristics.
wrelvo.why: Only where a sign allows it, on motorway sections with suitable design, can the limit rise to 150 km/h.

15d77bm.q: Unless otherwise signposted, the maximum permitted speed on motorways is 130 km/h.
15d77bm.why: The standard motorway limit is 130 km/h unless signs say otherwise.

1gojca5.q: Unless otherwise signposted, the maximum permitted speed in built-up areas is 50 km/h.
1gojca5.why: In built-up areas (centri abitati) the standard limit is 50 km/h unless signs say otherwise.

sp52gu.q: Unless otherwise signposted, the maximum permitted speed for mopeds is 45 km/h.

whu7am.q: Unless otherwise signposted, the maximum permitted speed for agricultural machines and operating machines with tyres is 40 km/h.
whu7am.why: Agricultural and operating machines fitted with tyres are limited to 40 km/h.

kk2n6.q: Unless otherwise signposted, the maximum permitted speed on motorways is 110 km/h in the rain.
kk2n6.why: In rain the motorway limit drops from 130 to 110 km/h.

1114jkb.q: Unless otherwise signposted, the maximum permitted speed on main extra-urban roads is 90 km/h in the event of hail.
1114jkb.why: In rain or hail the limit on main extra-urban roads drops from 110 to 90 km/h.

ydlrhm.q: Where specific signs are present, the maximum permitted speed in built-up areas on roads with particular characteristics is 70 km/h.
ydlrhm.why: Only where signs allow it, on urban roads with special design features, can the limit be raised to 70 km/h.

lyktgb.q: Unless otherwise signposted, the maximum permitted speed on main extra-urban roads is 110 km/h.
lyktgb.why: The standard limit on main extra-urban roads (strade extraurbane principali) is 110 km/h.

16ckg3l.q: On main extra-urban roads the maximum speed limit is 110 km/h for cars.
16ckg3l.why: Cars may travel up to 110 km/h on main extra-urban roads.

1uzt5x4.q: On main extra-urban roads the maximum speed limit is 70 km/h for a car towing a 900 kg caravan.
1uzt5x4.why: A car towing a caravan may not exceed 70 km/h on main extra-urban roads.

kdpmrn.q: On main extra-urban roads the maximum speed limit is 110 km/h for motor vehicles up to 3.5 t.
kdpmrn.why: Motor vehicles up to 3.5 t follow the ordinary limit of 110 km/h on main extra-urban roads.

1bbivlg.q: On main extra-urban roads the maximum speed limit is 70 km/h for articulated or combination lorries (autotreni).
1bbivlg.why: Lorry-and-trailer combinations (autotreni) are limited to 70 km/h on main extra-urban roads.

1easy5e.q: Unless otherwise signposted, the maximum permitted speed on urban roads is 80 km/h.
1easy5e.why: The standard limit on urban roads is 50 km/h; 80 km/h does not apply.

lqm1v6.q: Unless otherwise signposted, the maximum permitted speed for heavy quadricycles (quadricicli non leggeri) is 70 km/h.
lqm1v6.why: Heavy quadricycles (quadricicli non leggeri) may travel at up to 80 km/h outside built-up areas, not 70.

1not7ia.q: The maximum speed limit on any motorway is 150 km/h.
1not7ia.why: The normal limit is 130 km/h; 150 km/h applies only on suitable sections where a sign allows it.

5x3lak.q: On main extra-urban roads the maximum speed limit is 100 km/h for lorries (autocarri) with a gross mass of up to 3.5 t.
5x3lak.why: Up to 3.5 t the limit on main extra-urban roads is 110 km/h, not 100.

1f52bl5.q: On main extra-urban roads the maximum speed limit is 100 km/h for motorhomes (autocaravan) with a gross mass of up to 3.5 t.
1f52bl5.why: Motorhomes (autocaravan) up to 3.5 t may go up to 110 km/h on main extra-urban roads, not 100.

8z11wp.q: On main extra-urban roads the maximum speed limit is 80 km/h for cars with a light trailer.
8z11wp.why: With any trailer, even a light one, the limit on main extra-urban roads is 70 km/h.

5d08uw.q: On main extra-urban roads the maximum speed limit is 100 km/h for motorcycles.
5d08uw.why: Motorcycles may travel at 110 km/h on main extra-urban roads, not 100.

b7jqgf.q: On main extra-urban roads the maximum speed limit is 100 km/h for cars with a light trailer (carrello appendice).
b7jqgf.why: With a light appendage trailer (carrello appendice) the normal limit of 110 km/h applies, not 100.

1kt9emo.q: The maximum speed limit on secondary extra-urban roads is 90 km/h for motorcycles.
1kt9emo.why: Motorcycles may travel up to 90 km/h on secondary extra-urban roads.

jszp50.q: The maximum speed limit on secondary extra-urban roads is 90 km/h for cars with a light trailer (carrello appendice).
jszp50.why: A light appendage trailer (carrello appendice) does not reduce the limit: it stays 90 km/h on secondary extra-urban roads.

14q7rkn.q: The maximum speed limit on secondary extra-urban roads is 70 km/h for cars with a trailer for carrying boats or similar.
14q7rkn.why: With any trailer, including a boat trailer, the limit on secondary extra-urban roads is 70 km/h.

rtea37.q: The maximum speed limit on secondary extra-urban roads is 90 km/h for motorhomes (autocaravan) with a gross mass of up to 3.5 t.
rtea37.why: Motorhomes (autocaravan) up to 3.5 t follow the ordinary limit of 90 km/h on secondary extra-urban roads.

ewc65w.q: The maximum speed limit on secondary extra-urban roads is 90 km/h for lorries (autocarri) with a gross mass of up to 3.5 t.
ewc65w.why: Lorries up to 3.5 t may travel at 90 km/h on secondary extra-urban roads.

w5tdmu.q: The maximum speed limit on secondary extra-urban roads is 70 km/h for articulated or combination lorries (autotreni).
w5tdmu.why: Lorry-and-trailer combinations (autotreni) are limited to 70 km/h on secondary extra-urban roads.

1ow3nco.q: The maximum speed limit on secondary extra-urban roads is 70 km/h for mopeds.
1ow3nco.why: Mopeds (ciclomotori) may not exceed 45 km/h on any road.

spkn60.q: The maximum speed limit on secondary extra-urban roads is 90 km/h for heavy quadricycles (quadricicli non leggeri).
spkn60.why: Heavy quadricycles (quadricicli non leggeri) are limited to 80 km/h outside built-up areas, not 90.

1rlfxgj.q: The maximum speed limit on secondary extra-urban roads is 80 km/h for motorcycles.
1rlfxgj.why: Motorcycles may go up to 90 km/h on secondary extra-urban roads, not 80.

1405qe.q: The maximum speed limit on secondary extra-urban roads is 100 km/h for cars.
1405qe.why: The limit for cars on secondary extra-urban roads is 90 km/h, not 100.

15pew6g.q: The maximum speed limit on secondary extra-urban roads is 80 km/h for a car towing a 750 kg caravan.
15pew6g.why: When towing a caravan the limit on secondary extra-urban roads is 70 km/h, not 80.

f6b79m.q: The maximum speed limit on secondary extra-urban roads is 100 km/h for motor vehicles up to 3.5 tonnes.
f6b79m.why: Up to 3.5 t the limit on secondary extra-urban roads is 90 km/h, not 100.

1ucicwr.q: On secondary extra-urban roads the maximum speed limit is 80 km/h for cars with a light trailer (carrello appendice).
1ucicwr.why: With a light appendage trailer (carrello appendice) the normal limit of 90 km/h applies, not 80.

izwk5u.q: The markings shown in the figure are applied to the rear of certain categories of vehicles.
izwk5u.why: These discs showing 60, 80 and 100 are rear speed-limit stickers fitted to certain categories of vehicle, such as some buses.

1t2ev3o.q: The markings shown in the figure indicate the maximum speeds permitted for the vehicle on which they are applied.
1t2ev3o.why: The numbers 60, 80 and 100 show the maximum speed allowed for the vehicle carrying the sticker.

1vg4ms5.q: The markings shown in the figure are applied to some buses.
1vg4ms5.why: The 60, 80 and 100 speed stickers are fitted to the rear of some buses.

zdoloe.q: Speed must be reduced in mixed traffic (presence of slow and fast vehicles, or animals and pedestrians occupying the road).
zdoloe.why: In mixed traffic, or with animals and pedestrians on the road, you must reduce your speed.

d7fakg.q: Speed must be regulated according to the condition of the road surface (potholes, uneven patches, wet leaves).
d7fakg.why: Potholes, uneven surfaces or wet leaves reduce grip, so speed must match the road surface.

1gghy6m.q: The markings shown in the figure are applied to lorries (autocarri) with a gross mass of up to 3.5 tonnes.
1gghy6m.why: These stickers are not fitted to lorries up to 3.5 t, which follow the ordinary limits.

1f1vws.q: The markings shown in the figure are applied to motorhomes (autocaravan) with a total mass of up to 3.5 tonnes.
1f1vws.why: Motorhomes up to 3.5 t follow the ordinary limits and do not carry these stickers.

1mk4vmv.q: The markings shown in the figure are applied to motorcycles with an engine capacity above 150 cm3.
1mk4vmv.why: Motorcycles do not carry rear speed stickers; they follow the ordinary limits.

6kmy6z.q: Speed must be particularly moderate near a junction.
6kmy6z.why: The risk of conflict is high near a junction, so speed must be especially moderate.

1dyzl55.q: Speed must be particularly moderate in narrow stretches of road (strettoie).
1dyzl55.why: Space is limited in narrow stretches (strettoie), so you must be especially moderate in speed.

7906u3.q: Speed must be particularly moderate when it is difficult to pass other vehicles.
7906u3.why: When passing oncoming vehicles is difficult, you must be especially moderate in speed.

j21q5g.q: Speed must be particularly moderate on stretches of road where visibility is lacking (bends, humps).
j21q5g.why: Where you cannot see ahead, such as in bends or over humps, you must be especially moderate in speed.

l7lgmu.q: Speed must be particularly moderate when, where there are no sidewalks, pedestrians are on the carriageway.
l7lgmu.why: Without a sidewalk (marciapiede), pedestrians walk on the road and are vulnerable, so you must keep your speed very low to avoid them.

kypkto.q: You must reduce speed when the road is slippery because of water, snow, ice, leaves or mud.
kypkto.why: A slippery surface reduces grip and lengthens braking distance, so you must slow down.

1fd2nf3.q: Speed must be particularly moderate immediately after sunset.
1fd2nf3.why: The Code requires no special reduction just after sunset; you adapt speed to the actual visibility, not to the time of day.

vntqa5.q: Speed must be particularly moderate immediately after an intersection.
vntqa5.why: Extra caution is required when approaching and crossing intersections (incroci), not right after you have passed them.

1v3er38.q: You must adjust your speed according to the driver's hurry.
1v3er38.why: Speed depends on road, traffic, visibility and vehicle conditions, never on how much of a hurry the driver is in.

c6igaf.q: You must keep a speed suited only to our own health conditions.
c6igaf.why: Speed must suit all conditions: road, traffic, visibility, vehicle and load, not just the driver's own health.

19yy55n.q: You must always keep a speed above 30 km/h.
19yy55n.why: There is no rule to always exceed 30 km/h; you adapt speed to conditions and may need to drive slower.

1ehyhah.q: You must reduce speed when you are being followed by a scheduled bus.
1ehyhah.why: Being followed by a scheduled bus (autobus di linea) does not oblige you to slow down; you slow down only for road and traffic conditions.

zrta8i.q: You must adjust your speed according to the state of maintenance and cleanliness of the road.
zrta8i.why: Potholes, dirt or a poor surface affect grip and control, so you must adapt your speed to the road condition.

bmrh3z.q: Speed must be reduced in case of strong crosswind.
bmrh3z.why: A strong crosswind can push the vehicle off course; slowing down helps you keep control.

11948z0.q: Speed must be reduced when dazzled by the sun.
11948z0.why: Glare from the sun reduces visibility, so you must slow down to have time to see and react.

1pv31s8.q: On motorways and main extra-urban roads, in dense fog with visibility under 100 m, temporary maximum speed limits of no more than 50 km/h may be imposed.
1pv31s8.why: In dense fog with visibility under 100 m, temporary limits of up to 50 km/h at most may be set on these roads.

14z1b7e.q: Unless otherwise signed, the maximum speed limit on main extra-urban roads is 100 km/h.
14z1b7e.why: On main extra-urban roads (strade extraurbane principali) the limit is 110 km/h, not 100.

1gnyewa.q: Unless otherwise signed, the maximum speed limit in built-up areas is 60 km/h, valid up to one kilometre after leaving the town.
1gnyewa.why: In built-up areas (centri abitati) the limit is 50 km/h and applies only up to the end-of-town sign.

ekw2ns.q: You must reduce speed every time you meet an information sign.
ekw2ns.why: Information signs (segnali di indicazione) only give guidance and do not require you to slow down.

1bk0gcd.q: On motorways, the maximum speed limit is 80 km/h for cars towing a horse trailer.
1bk0gcd.why: A car towing a trailer may not exceed 80 km/h on a motorway.

1lees0c.q: The maximum speed limit on secondary extra-urban roads is 70 km/h for cars towing a trailer for carrying motorcycles.
1lees0c.why: A car towing a trailer is limited to 70 km/h on extra-urban roads.

11vbvge.q: You must regulate your speed in particular when roadworks are in progress.
11vbvge.why: Roadworks mean narrowed lanes, workers and uneven surfaces, so you must adapt your speed.

wgdvo7.q: You must regulate your speed in particular if you meet the stopped-vehicle sign (movable danger triangle) on the road.
wgdvo7.why: The triangle warns of a stopped vehicle that is a hazard, so you must slow down and be ready to go around it.

bu2zek.q: When travelling in parallel lanes, it is possible for traffic in the right lane to move faster than in the left lane.
bu2zek.why: In parallel-lane traffic (file parallele) the right lane may move faster than the left, and this is not counted as overtaking.

4cdvwp.q: Along channelling lanes, it is possible for traffic in the right lane to move faster than in the left lane.
4cdvwp.why: With channelled traffic, lanes can move at different speeds, including a faster right lane.

h4r2fg.q: When traffic is channelled, it is possible for traffic in the right lane to move faster than in the left lane.
h4r2fg.why: When traffic is channelled into lanes, the right lane can legitimately move faster than the left.

x9e8hp.q: On four-lane motorways it is permitted to travel up to 170 km/h.
x9e8hp.why: The motorway maximum is 130 km/h (150 km/h only where signed and permitted), never 170.

a825b6.q: On motorways it is permitted to exceed 130 km/h at night, provided high-beam headlights are used.
a825b6.why: The 130 km/h limit always applies; using high beams does not raise it.

1cfkj00.q: On a motorway, in the overtaking lane, it is not permitted to exceed 110 km/h.
1cfkj00.why: The overtaking lane has no special limit; the general motorway limit of 130 km/h applies.

1vmbls6.q: On motorways, the maximum speed limit is 150 km/h in daytime and 130 km/h at night.
1vmbls6.why: The limit is 130 km/h day and night; 150 km/h applies only on sections where it is signed.

1enzdi4.q: On main extra-urban roads with particular construction and safety features, the maximum speed limit may be 130 km/h.
1enzdi4.why: On main extra-urban roads the limit cannot exceed 110 km/h; 130 km/h belongs to motorways.

h1w0p5.q: On main extra-urban roads it is permitted to exceed 110 km/h, but only on downhill stretches.
h1w0p5.why: The 110 km/h limit applies on downhill sections too and may not be exceeded.

1i758ym.q: The maximum speed limit on secondary extra-urban roads is 90 km/h for cars towing a trailer for carrying inflatable boats or gliders.
1i758ym.why: A car with a trailer is limited to 70 km/h on extra-urban roads, whatever the load.

87yaoe.q: On secondary extra-urban roads the maximum speed limit for agricultural machines and operating machines is 70 km/h if their flashing yellow light device is in operation.
87yaoe.why: Agricultural and operating machines have much lower limits, and the flashing yellow light does not raise them.

1lxc1jd.q: If you cross an intersection at high speed while having right of way, in case of an accident shared fault cannot be ruled out.
1lxc1jd.why: Having right of way does not excuse excessive speed, so you may share the fault (concorso di colpa) in a crash.

1mrml9v.q: The maximum speed limits in force on motorways and extra-urban roads are not identical in all European countries.
1mrml9v.why: Each country sets its own limits, so they differ across Europe.

1so6o1m.q: If you cross an intersection at high speed while having right of way, in case of an accident you are completely free of responsibility.
1so6o1m.why: A driver with right of way who goes too fast can still be held partly responsible.

1ge8p2x.q: If you cross at high speed an intersection where you have right of way, in case of an accident the responsibility will lie solely with the driver coming from the road without right of way.
1ge8p2x.why: Responsibility can be shared: the driver with right of way is also liable if speeding.

7rc916.q: If you cross an intersection with right of way, you have no obligation to slow down.
7rc916.why: Even with right of way you must moderate your speed when approaching intersections.

146b78h.q: If you cross at high speed an intersection with right of way, in case of an accident the responsibility will lie with the driver of the vehicle that entered the intersection first.
146b78h.why: Liability does not depend on who entered the intersection first, but on right of way, speed and caution.

16mf1vu.q: If a vehicle is forced to stop on the tracks of a level crossing, you must move it off the tracks as soon as possible by pushing it.
16mf1vu.why: A vehicle stuck on the tracks must be cleared at once, even by pushing it, to free the line.

aoihp2.q: If a vehicle is forced to stop on the tracks of a level crossing and cannot be moved immediately, you must have everyone on board get out immediately and notify the railway station.
aoihp2.why: If the vehicle cannot be moved right away, everyone must get out and the railway station must be notified.

1476f22.q: If a vehicle is forced to stop on the railway tracks of a level crossing, you must make sure that train drivers are warned of the danger in good time.
1476f22.why: You must do what you can to warn approaching train drivers early enough.

1nuty59.q: If you go down a long descent in neutral with the engine off, steering becomes difficult if the vehicle has power steering.
1nuty59.why: With the engine off, power steering (servosterzo) gives no assistance, so the steering becomes heavy.

phl6xm.q: If you go down a long descent in neutral with the engine off, braking becomes difficult if the vehicle has a brake servo.
phl6xm.why: With the engine off, the brake servo (servofreno) loses its vacuum and braking needs much more effort.

1ylmsds.q: In vehicles with a brake servo, going down a long descent in neutral with the engine off increases the risk of causing accidents.
1ylmsds.why: Without servo assistance braking is less effective, so the risk of accidents increases.

17993rk.q: In vehicles with power steering, going down a long descent in neutral with the engine off makes it difficult to turn the steering wheel quickly to avoid an obstacle.
17993rk.why: Without active power steering it is hard to turn quickly to dodge an obstacle.

1fd0rq3.q: In vehicles with a brake servo, going down a long descent in neutral with the engine off dangerously increases the braking distance.
1fd0rq3.why: With the servo inactive, the pedal needs more force and the braking distance grows dangerously.

1wj8bbt.q: In vehicles with a brake servo, going down a long descent in neutral with the engine off makes it more and more difficult to stop the vehicle.
1wj8bbt.why: Each brake application uses up the remaining servo assistance, so stopping gets harder and harder.

1duzx7f.q: If you go down a long descent in neutral with the engine off, there is an electrical current overload.
1duzx7f.why: A switched-off engine does not cause electrical overload; the problem is loss of brake and steering assistance.

1npnoq1.q: If you go down a long descent in neutral with the engine off, a differential malfunction may occur.
1npnoq1.why: The differential is not affected this way; the risks concern brakes and steering.

1refvdu.q: For greater safety, it is advisable to go down long descents in neutral with the engine off, thereby also saving fuel.
1refvdu.why: This is dangerous: you lose engine braking and brake and steering assistance. Descend with a gear engaged.

1olokil.q: If you go down a long descent in neutral with the engine off, it is advisable to remove the ignition key.
1olokil.why: Removing the key can lock the steering, which is extremely dangerous, so you should never do it.

ci2131.q: In vehicles with a vacuum brake servo, going down a long descent in neutral with the engine off gives the same braking force as with the engine on.
ci2131.why: With the engine off the vacuum is used up, so braking force is lower than with the engine running.

1rgqudf.q: In a built-up area, if you see a ball rolling onto the carriageway, you must reduce speed immediately.
1rgqudf.why: A ball suggests a child may follow, so you must slow down immediately.

dcro3n.q: In a built-up area, if you see a ball rolling onto the carriageway, you must slow down so as to be able to stop if necessary.
dcro3n.why: You slow down so that you can stop in time if a child appears.

7vce0c.q: In a built-up area, if you see a ball rolling onto the carriageway, you must also anticipate a child possibly crossing the road.
7vce0c.why: A child often runs after a ball, so you must expect them to cross.

1h3w5wv.q: In a built-up area, if you see a ball rolling onto the carriageway, you must slow down progressively, to avoid being hit from behind by the following vehicle.
1h3w5wv.why: Slowing gradually avoids a rear-end collision with the vehicle behind.

443r9v.q: In a built-up area, if you see a ball rolling onto the carriageway, you must swerve sharply.
443r9v.why: Sharp swerving risks losing control and creating new hazards; brake in a controlled way instead.

11vlwuv.q: On a two-way road, if you see a ball rolling onto the carriageway, you must dodge it, even by entering the opposite lane.
11vlwuv.why: Moving into the opposite lane endangers oncoming traffic; slow down and be ready to stop.

10nsv6k.q: In a built-up area, if you see a ball rolling onto the carriageway, there is no need to slow down, to avoid being hit from behind by the following vehicle.
10nsv6k.why: You must slow down anyway, progressively; fear of being rear-ended is no reason not to.

1yh04yg.q: In a built-up area, if you see a ball rolling onto the carriageway, you must immediately activate the hazard warning lights.
1yh04yg.why: Hazard lights are not needed here; simply slow down carefully.

s69u79.q: Passing very close to a parked car that still has people on board can be dangerous, because of the possible careless opening of the doors.
s69u79.why: Occupants may open a door suddenly and hit you as you pass close by.

1xvdjw9.q: It can be dangerous to drive too close to parked cars, because they may block the view of a person in a wheelchair or a pedestrian pushing a pram who is about to cross.
1xvdjw9.why: Parked cars can hide vulnerable pedestrians about to cross, so you should keep your distance.

17qj0qr.q: Passing very close to a parked car that still has people on board is not a serious danger if done at low speed.
17qj0qr.why: A suddenly opened door is dangerous even at low speed; leave enough side clearance.

v14rk0.q: Passing very close to a parked car that still has people on board is dangerous only if one of the doors is already open.
v14rk0.why: The danger exists with closed doors too, since they can open suddenly.

z9d6bd.q: Passing very close to a parked car that still has people on board is dangerous only if the driver and some passengers have already got out.
z9d6bd.why: The danger exists even when everyone is still inside, as anyone can open a door.

1py20h4.q: Passing very close to a parked car that still has people on board can be dangerous only if you are travelling at high speed.
1py20h4.why: The risk of hitting an opening door is not only a matter of speed; always leave side clearance.

31x9nk.q: If, at a level crossing, you are still on the tracks with your vehicle when the barriers begin to close, you must stay calm and clear the railway line by any means.
31x9nk.why: Stay calm and get off the railway line immediately by any means.

yut647.q: If, at a level crossing, you are still on the tracks with your vehicle when the barriers begin to close, you must clear the railway line by any means, if necessary even breaking through the barriers.
yut647.why: You must clear the line by any means, even breaking through the barriers if necessary.

1r96pm9.q: If, because of a breakdown, you are stuck on the railway line at a level crossing, you must work to remove the vehicle as soon as possible, for example by being towed by other road users.
1r96pm9.why: The vehicle must be removed as soon as possible, even by being towed by other users.

1vppo83.q: If, because of a breakdown of your car, you are stuck on the railway line at a level crossing, you must work to remove the vehicle as soon as possible, for example by getting other users to help push it off the line.
1vppo83.why: You can ask others to help push the vehicle off the tracks right away.

ow4mwm.q: At level crossings you must use maximum caution and moderate your speed, to avoid dangerous situations that would damage the equipment.
ow4mwm.why: Caution and moderate speed prevent damage to the crossing equipment.

1o6o3wk.q: At level crossings you must use maximum caution and moderate your speed, to avoid dangerous situations that would result in a collision with the crossing's barriers.
1o6o3wk.why: Moderate speed and caution prevent collisions with the barriers.

6bfije.q: Crossing a level crossing without respecting all the rules can endanger the safety of many people travelling on a passing train.
6bfije.why: A violation can cause a serious accident with the train, endangering many passengers.

11f2xxq.q: Crossing a level crossing with a reckless manoeuvre to save time can be a danger to many people, as well as to the driver.
11f2xxq.why: A reckless manoeuvre endangers train passengers too, not just the driver.

169l28l.q: If a vehicle remains stopped between the closed barriers of a level crossing, you must do everything possible to warn any approaching trains of the danger.
169l28l.why: You must do everything possible to warn approaching trains in advance.

1guhdwk.q: If, at a level crossing, you are still on the tracks with your vehicle when the barriers begin to close, you must get out and quickly abandon the vehicle to reach safety.
1guhdwk.why: You must clear the tracks with the vehicle, not abandon it on the line.

14ni7wq.q: If, at a level crossing, you are still on the tracks with your vehicle when the barriers begin to close, and you are towing a trailer, you must quickly unhook it and abandon it on the tracks to save at least the towing vehicle.
14ni7wq.why: The trailer must also be cleared off the line; leaving it on the tracks is dangerous.

746mej.q: If, because of a breakdown, you are stuck on the railway line of a level crossing, you must quickly unload the vehicle to save at least the cargo.
746mej.why: The priority is to clear the tracks and protect people, not to save the cargo.

sx7ham.q: If, because of a breakdown of your car, you are stuck on the railway line of a level crossing, you must quickly empty the fuel tank to avoid fire in case of collision with the train.
sx7ham.why: Emptying the tank is not required and wastes time: get people out, remove the vehicle and give warning.

1ubuqxf.q: Level crossings must be approached at very high speed to avoid getting stuck on the railway line.
1ubuqxf.why: Approach them at moderate speed and only if the road beyond is clear, so you don't get stuck.

1l1cksl.q: Level crossings must be approached at very high speed to be able to break through the barriers if you cannot stop in time with the barriers lowered.
1l1cksl.why: High speed is dangerous and no excuse for breaking barriers; slow down so you can stop in time.

17fo73r.q: Crossing a level crossing without respecting all the rules entails only a minor administrative fine, as it poses no real danger to other users.
17fo73r.why: Breaking level crossing rules is very dangerous, with serious penalties and risk to many people.

17h85g8.q: Crossing a level crossing with a reckless manoeuvre to save time can be dangerous only at night.
17h85g8.why: A reckless manoeuvre is dangerous at any hour, day or night.

1ihu9r4.q: If a vehicle remains stopped between the closed barriers of a level crossing, the driver's only obligation is to switch off the engine and ask any passengers to get out.
1ihu9r4.why: Besides getting passengers out, you must remove the vehicle and warn approaching trains.

wegz2q.q: If a vehicle remains stopped between the closed barriers of a level crossing, you must move away at least one hundred metres as soon as possible.
wegz2q.why: There is no 100 m rule: get people out, try to remove the vehicle and give warning.

3zawfs.q: In the event of a collision between vehicles at a level crossing, vehicles must not be moved off the tracks if there are injured people.
3zawfs.why: The train danger means the tracks must be cleared: people, and vehicles if possible, must be moved away.
